findings.problem: Both proofs separately derive the pointwise formula for coindBasisMap on a finite sum of basis-weighted components. Each proves that the map equals a Finset sum of coindLine terms (hexp in the injectivity proof, hx in the surjectivity proof). Each then applies coind_sum_eval and coindLine_apply to get (coindBasisMap V b x) r = ∑ j ∈ s, (x j) r • b j. The two blocks differ only in how the DFinsupp is written: φ over φ.support, versus ∑ single over s. This is a core structural fact about coindBasisMap, but it is re-proved inline each time with different simp sets.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma after coindBasisMap and before the injectivity proof, with the same implicit and explicit variables as coindBasisMap_injective:

lemma coindBasisMap_apply (V : ModuleCat.{u} k) (b : Basis ι k V) (x : Π₀ _ : ι, DA k R) (s : Finset ι) (hs : x.support ⊆ s) (r : R) :
    coindBasisMap V b x r = ∑ j ∈ s, x j r • b j

Proof sketch:
1. Rewrite x as ∑ j ∈ s, DFinsupp.single j (x j), using DFinsupp.sum_single or DFinsupp.sum_eq_sum_fintype together with hs.
2. Push coindBasisMap through the sum with map_sum, and use DFinsupp.lsum_single to get coindLine V (b j) (x j).
3. Finish with coind_sum_eval and coindLine_apply.

In the injectivity proof, replace he with `coindBasisMap_apply V b φ φ.support subset_rfl r`. In the surjectivity proof, apply the lemma to x := ∑ i ∈ s, DFinsupp.single i (c i). This needs the support inclusion for that x, which follows from DFinsupp.support_finset_sum_subset or an equivalent. The result is ∑ j ∈ s, x j r • b j. To reach the current he, rewrite x j as c j with a lemma for the value of the sum of singles (DFinsupp.finset_sum_apply together with DFinsupp.single_apply). The existing Finset.sum_congr … rfl then identifies c i r with b.repr (φ r) i. Alternatively, state the lemma only for x = ∑ i ∈ s, single i (c i), with c : ι → DA k R. The injectivity case follows from φ = ∑ j ∈ φ.support, single j (φ j). This removes the need for a support hypothesis.
findings.benefit: The unfolding of lsum, the coind_sum_eval step and the coindLine_apply step are written and maintained once. Both proofs then read as the mathematical argument: compare coordinates via b.repr for injectivity, and build the preimage from the finite support for surjectivity. A change to coindBasisMap or coindLine needs one repair instead of two separate simp-set repairs.
